Truebill launched in 2015 as a subscription cancellation tool. Co-founders Haroon and Yahya Mokhtarzada, along with Edward Tian, built it in Silver Spring, Maryland, with a simple premise: most people don’t know exactly how many subscriptions they’re paying for each month, and Truebill would answer that in about five minutes.

Rocket’s strategic logic was clear: a fintech app with millions of users who’ve already linked their bank accounts is a useful channel for other financial products. If you’re managing subscriptions inside Rocket Money, you’re one tap from a mortgage rate check or a personal loan offer through Rocket’s connected products.

For Truebill’s founders, the $1.275 billion cash price was roughly 2.4x the company’s last private valuation of $530 million. All existing user accounts carried over to the new brand. The team stayed on and continued running the product.

Pricing stayed in roughly the same range. Rocket Money Premium costs $6–$12/month on a pay-what-you-think-is-fair model, which is how Truebill structured its paid tier as well. The bill negotiation service still takes 35–60% of first-year savings, same as before.

For most people, this is the same trade-off they’ve already accepted with other banking and budgeting apps. Rocket Money has a documented privacy policy covering data retention and third-party data sharing, and the Plaid connection is the standard mechanism for consumer fintech.
For a full breakdown of Rocket Money’s Plaid permissions, data retention practices, and what it shares with third parties, see our

The limits on the free plan are real, though. You can’t request cancellations through the app; that’s a Premium feature. Budget categories cap at 2, which makes any detailed tracking impractical. Credit score monitoring and the Smart Savings automation tool are both paid-only.
The app holds a 4.5-star rating on the App Store and 4.6 on Google Play across 400,000+ combined reviews as of 2026. It’s a large, actively maintained product with a real user base.

실제로 저 자신도 12개의 서비스에 가입되어 있지만, 관리가 제대로 되지 않아 해지하는 것을 잊고 서비스 비용을 계속 지불하거나, 계정을 중복으로 생성하는 등 다양한 실수를 반복해 왔습니다.
이번에는 저처럼 구독 관리가 제대로 되지 않는 분들께 추천하고 싶은 미국 스타트업 Trubill을 소개합니다.
Trubill은 개인을 위한 구독 관리 기능을 제공하는 앱입니다. 은행 계좌와 신용카드를 Trubill과 연동하여 데이터를 수집하고, 가입된 구독 서비스를 관리합니다. 아래에 Trubill의 특징을 간단히 정리합니다.
사용자가 가입한 구독 서비스를 목록으로 표시합니다. 저는 12개의 서비스를 이용하고 있는데, Trubill은 그중 10개를 인식하여 지금까지의 지불 금액, 지불일 등을 시각화해 주었습니다. 그 외에도 가입한 구독을 Trubill 앱에서 바로 취소할 수 있는 점도 편리합니다.
